key_insight: Pion updates each weight matrix via left and right orthogonal transformations that preserve its singular values, changing matrix geometry without altering its spectrum. This yields optimization that modulates singular vectors while keeping spectral norms fixed.
problem_solved: Additive optimizers (e.g., Adam) change singular values and spectral norms during training, which can harm conditioning, stability, and predictable geometry of large weight matrices; Pion addresses this by preserving the spectrum of every weight matrix throughout optimization.
method: Formulate weight updates as orthogonal equivalence transformations: W <- U W V^T, where U and V are orthogonal transforms derived from gradient information.
Derive an update rule that computes these left/right orthogonal factors so that singular values of W remain unchanged while singular vectors are adjusted.
Apply the transforms per weight matrix to modulate geometry (rotations/reflections of subspaces) without changing spectral norms, enabling spectrum-preserving optimization during LLM training.
impact: By keeping singular values fixed, Pion can improve numerical stability, control Lipschitz/spectral properties, and give more predictable conditioning during large-model training—potentially improving robustness and reproducibility for LLM practitioners.
visual_elements: Before/after SVD diagram: show W = UΣV^T with identical singular-value bars but rotated singular vectors after a Pion update.
Update flowchart: gradient → compute orthogonal factors U,V → apply W ← U W V^T (highlight spectrum preservation step).
Line chart comparing spectral-norm trajectories across training for Adam vs Pion (Pion flat, Adam varying).
Geometric illustration: matrix as ellipsoid where Pion rotates the ellipsoid without changing axis lengths (singular values).
paper_title: Pion: A Spectrum-Preserving Optimizer via Orthogonal Equivalence Transformation
paper_authors: Kexuan Shi, Hanxuan Li, Zeju Qiu, Yandong Wen, Simon Buchholz
